writing.prompt: Directions: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university canteens should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.sample: Recently, our university has been collecting opinions on whether campus canteens should welcome outside visitors. In my view, opening them to the public is a wise move that benefits both the campus and the community.For one thing, university canteens usually offer clean and affordable meals, so opening them can relieve the dining pressure faced by nearby residents and office workers who struggle to find cheap lunches. For another, the extra income earned from these visitors allows canteens to upgrade their equipment and even lower prices for students. Admittedly, more diners may cause crowding and raise safety concerns; however, such problems can be eased by setting fixed visiting hours and checking visitors at the gate.Therefore, I firmly believe that a properly managed open canteen is worthwhile. As long as student needs come first, sharing this resource makes our university a warmer part of society.

transcript.en: A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird. The flight from Palm Beach International Airport to LaGuardia Airport turned around just minutes after takeoff following the strike.
transcript.zh: JetBlue航空公司一架从西棕榈滩飞往纽约市的航班周日上午在飞机撞鸟后被迫掉头降落。这架从棕榈滩国际机场飞往LaGuardia机场的航班在起飞仅几分钟后因撞击事件而掉头返航。

transcript.en: No injuries were reported on the plane, and the flight took off once again 7.5 hours after the first attempt. "It was like a split second of panic…that resulted in this nervous reaction on the plane," said passenger Brian Healy. "There was total quiet, and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop." An email from JetBlue read, "Our team is working to accommodate customers on later flights."
transcript.zh: 机上未报告有人员受伤,该航班在首次尝试起飞7.5小时后再次起飞。乘客Brian Healy说:"那就像一瞬间的恐慌……导致机上出现紧张反应。机舱内一片寂静,当飞机停下来时大家才松了口气。"JetBlue发送的一封电子邮件写道:"我们的团队正在努力为乘客安排后续航班。"

transcript.en: A deadly snake, which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo, has slipped away for the second time. The poisonous snake forced the closure of the attraction last week when staff noticed the disappearance.
transcript.zh: 一条致命的毒蛇在从动物园逃脱后终于被追踪到,却第二次溜走了。上周当工作人员注意到这条毒蛇失踪时,它迫使该景点关闭。

transcript.en: After six days of desperate searching, he was eventually found and placed in a supposedly secure area. But it seems the animal is no fan of the zoo, because yet again he is out on the loose. The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo but has already been frustrating its staff. The staff believe he squeezed himself out of a gap located around new energy-saving bulbs installed inside the snake house. He was only found the first time around because staff brought in a special machine to trace him inside a wall opening.
transcript.zh: 经过六天的拼命搜寻,它最终被找到并被安置在一个据称安全的区域。但这只动物似乎并不喜欢这家动物园,因为它再次逃脱了。这条蛇是动物园相对较新的成员,但已经让工作人员感到沮丧。工作人员认为它是从蛇舍内安装的新型节能灯泡周围的缝隙中挤出去的。它第一次被找到是因为工作人员带来了一台特殊的机器,在墙壁开口内追踪到了它。

transcript.en: This kind of snake is one of the most deadly and poisonous in the wild, and they can range from 3 to 5 meters in length.
transcript.zh: 这种蛇是野外最致命、毒性最强的蛇类之一,体长可达3至5米。

transcript.en: Electric bikes have been the craze in downtown Jacksonville since they were first introduced earlier this month as a one-year pilot program. But they're leading to safety concerns, mainly at night when some riders don't follow the rules of the road.
transcript.zh: 自本月早些时候作为为期一年的试点项目首次引入以来,电动自行车在杰克逊维尔市中心引发了热潮。但它们引发了安全担忧,主要是在夜间,一些骑行者不遵守交通规则。

transcript.en: As the night goes on, groups of riders are often seen traveling in just about every direction in the streets and on pedestrian paths. That is increasing the probability of dangerous accidents.
transcript.zh: 随着夜幕降临,经常可以看到成群的骑行者在街道和人行道上几乎朝着各个方向行驶。这增加了发生危险事故的可能性。

transcript.en: Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile. That means no running red lights or traveling in the opposite direction of traffic on one-way streets.
transcript.zh: 电动自行车骑行者必须遵守与驾驶汽车时相同的所有规则。这意味着不能闯红灯,也不能在单行道上逆向行驶。

transcript.en: City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown. And she's aware of the concerns. Cumber said, "People can have fun, but both drivers and riders are responsible for paying attention while on the road. And never assume the driver is going to stop or see you."
transcript.zh: 市议会成员Anna Cumber在将电动自行车引入杰克逊维尔以为市中心注入新活力方面发挥了重要作用。她也意识到了这些担忧。Cumber说:"人们可以享受乐趣,但驾驶员和骑行者都有责任在路上保持注意力。永远不要假设驾驶员会停车或看到你。"

transcript.en: M: What's the best way to teach children how to save and spend their money?
transcript.zh: M: 教孩子如何存钱和花钱,最好的方法是什么?

transcript.en: W: You should make money a regular topic of discussion. It's best to start young, so it's instinctive rather than a scary subject.
transcript.zh: W: 你应该把钱的话题作为日常讨论的内容。最好从小开始,这样就会成为本能反应,而不是一个可怕的话题。

transcript.en: M: In our family, we talk openly about things like the budget for holidays, how taxes reduce your income, and how to shop around for the best deals.
transcript.zh: M: 在我们家,我们公开讨论像假期预算、税收如何减少你的收入,以及如何货比三家找到最优惠的价格这类事情。

transcript.en: W: Indeed. It's also essential to make money real for children through practical examples. Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums.
transcript.zh: W: 确实如此。通过实际例子让孩子对金钱有真实感受也很重要。比如算出使用披萨折扣券能省多少钱,这比抽象的数字计算要实用得多。

transcript.en: M: We also give our kids pocket money, and the amount they get is linked to chores, such as putting the bins out and emptying the dishwasher.
transcript.zh: M: 我们还给孩子零花钱,金额多少跟家务挂钩,比如倒垃圾和清空洗碗机。

transcript.en: W: We do that too, and it's paid according to their age. Two pounds for each year so they can see some progression.
transcript.zh: W: 我们也这样做,而且是按年龄支付。每岁两英镑,这样他们能看到一些进步。

transcript.en: M: Teaching them to save is important. We opened a savings account when they were young. After birthdays and Christmas, they would go to the branch and deposit their gift money.
transcript.zh: M: 教他们存钱很重要。我们在他们小时候就开了储蓄账户。生日和圣诞节过后,他们会去银行网点存入收到的礼金。

transcript.en: W: Oh, I hadn't considered doing that. In our house, we have transparent money boxes for them to put small change in, so they can see their savings grow.
transcript.zh: W: 哦,我还没考虑过这样做。在我们家,我们有透明的存钱罐让他们放零钱,这样他们能看到自己的储蓄增长。

transcript.en: M: When the time is right, I'll start talking to our children about investing and show them how the money saved for their further education has grown.
transcript.zh: M: 时机成熟时,我会开始跟孩子们谈投资,让他们看看为他们继续教育存的钱是如何增长的。

transcript.en: W: I am always talking to my elder daughter about the importance of saving into a pension. She's just started a part-time job and was thinking of not contributing to her pension. Luckily, I managed to persuade her otherwise.
transcript.zh: W: 我一直跟大女儿强调存养老金的重要性。她刚开始做兼职,本来想着不缴纳养老金。幸好我说服了她。

transcript.en: M: Yes, it's such an important lesson to learn.
transcript.zh: M: 是的,这是非常重要的一课。

transcript.en: W: Your book has sold 2 million copies, but before we discuss why it's getting so much attention, let's talk about your background. You're an economist and spent two decades teaching at universities?
transcript.zh: W: 您的书已经售出200万册,但在我们讨论它为什么受到如此多关注之前,让我们先聊聊您的背景。您是一位经济学家,在大学教了二十年书?

transcript.en: M: I spent 25 years as a professor, actually. And then, for the last 10 years, I've worked as a political consultant, advising politicians at the national level about problems in our country.
transcript.zh: M: 实际上我当了25年教授。然后,在过去10年里,我一直担任政治顾问,就我们国家的问题向国家层面的政治家们提供建议。

transcript.en: W: You discuss three of those problems in the book, improving public education, reducing our nation's healthcare burden, and increasing personal savings. But your ideas about education are the most controversial.

transcript.en: M: Absolutely. A lot of people think I'm trying to punish students who aren't doing well, when actually my goal is to give all students more incentive to succeed.
transcript.zh: M: 没错。很多人认为我是在惩罚那些表现不好的学生,而实际上我的目标是给所有学生更多成功的动力。

transcript.en: W: I'm not sure I agree with you. Your proposal to pay cash rewards to students who get good grades is a particular problem. What about students who don't get good grades? It seems like you're blaming them for not succeeding, when poor performance in school isn't a child's fault.
transcript.zh: W: 我不确定我是否同意您的观点。您提议向成绩好的学生支付现金奖励,这是个特别的问题。那成绩不好的学生怎么办?看起来您是在责怪他们不成功,而在学校表现不佳并不是孩子的错。

transcript.en: M: But my proposal is not just to reward students with good grades, but also students who show improvements.
transcript.zh: M: 但我的提议不仅是奖励成绩好的学生,也奖励那些有进步的学生。

transcript.en: W: Okay, another criticism of the plan is the cash rewards themselves. Where will the money come from?
transcript.zh: W: 好吧,这个计划的另一个批评是现金奖励本身。钱从哪里来?

transcript.en: M: If students do better, we'll spend less on schooling. So, in the end, the rewards will pay for themselves.
transcript.zh: M: 如果学生们表现更好,我们在教育上的花费就会减少。所以,最终这些奖励会自己收回成本。

transcript.en: W: What about now? How will we fund the rewards in the meantime?
transcript.zh: W: 那现在呢?在此期间我们如何资助这些奖励?

transcript.en: M: Well, by increasing taxes or moving money from other areas of the budget into education.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯,通过增加税收或者从预算的其他领域把钱转移到教育上。

transcript.en: I met three different people today, and each time, when I asked, "How are you?" The reply was exactly the same. "I'm busy". Honestly, I hear the same answer from the vast majority of people I meet. So I started to think: "Guess what? Everybody's busy!" I'm busy, you're busy, everybody's busy. So you being busy doesn't make me sympathetic at all. Because "busy" is the state of the world.
transcript.zh: 我今天遇到了三个不同的人,每次当我问"你好吗?"时,得到的回答都一模一样。"我很忙"。老实说,我遇到的绝大多数人都给我同样的答案。所以我开始思考:"你猜怎么着?每个人都很忙!"我很忙,你很忙,每个人都很忙。所以你忙根本不会让我感到同情。因为"忙"就是这个世界的常态。

transcript.en: So I'm launching a campaign to stop people complaining about being "busy." It may sound harsh, but the truth is, nobody cares. In a busy world, "being busy" doesn't stand out, nor does it mean productive, creative, accomplished, or professional.
transcript.zh: 所以我正在发起一项运动,呼吁人们停止抱怨自己"很忙"。这听起来可能有点刺耳,但事实是,没有人在乎。在一个忙碌的世界里,"忙碌"并不突出,也不意味着高效、有创造力、有成就或专业。

transcript.en: Steve Maraboli once said, "When someone tells you they are too 'busy', it's not a reflection of their schedule; it's a reflection of YOUR spot on their schedule." Donna Lynn Hope has also remarked, "Busy doesn't mean better. I've never envied a busy person—the one who likes to point out their busy lives to others."
transcript.zh: Steve Maraboli曾经说过:"当有人告诉你他们太'忙'时,这不是反映他们的日程安排;而是反映了你在他们日程安排中的位置。"Donna Lynn Hope也评论道:"忙碌并不意味着更好。我从不羡慕忙碌的人——那种喜欢向别人强调自己生活有多忙的人。"

transcript.en: The reality is, nobody is too busy—it's just about priorities. So the next time someone asks you how you are, maybe respond differently. In my experience, the "I'm busy" response is really covering up the fact that they're not actually accomplishing their real purpose. And "being busy" is the lie they tell themselves about why they can't achieve it.
transcript.zh: 现实是,没有人真的太忙——这只是关乎优先级的问题。所以下次有人问你过得怎么样时,也许可以换一种回答方式。根据我的经验,"我很忙"这个回答实际上是在掩盖他们并没有真正完成自己真正目标的事实。而"忙碌"是他们对自己无法实现目标所撒的谎。

transcript.en: More and more people are taking up extreme sports, like snowboarding, skateboarding, mountain biking, and many more. Why are these sports becoming so popular?
transcript.zh: 越来越多的人开始从事极限运动,如滑雪板、滑板、山地自行车等等。为什么这些运动变得如此流行?

transcript.en: One thing that extreme sports do better than perhaps anything else is to help you stop being afraid. It may sound strange to say that their main function is to reduce fear. But after a time, your fear response to other things in life will be dramatically reduced. After all, if you can jump out of a plane or off a bridge, then you can face anything else easily.
transcript.zh: 极限运动比其他任何事物都更能帮助你克服恐惧。说它们的主要功能是减少恐惧可能听起来很奇怪。但一段时间后,你对生活中其他事物的恐惧反应将会大幅减少。毕竟,如果你能从飞机上或桥上跳下来,那么你就能轻松面对其他任何事情。

transcript.en: When doing extreme sports, you have to become more focused. You'll be pushed to your limits, and if you aren't focused you'll make dangerous mistakes. Learning to be this focused when enjoying extreme sports will help you to be focused at work, keeping you more productive and ultimately more successful.
transcript.zh: 在进行极限运动时,你必须变得更加专注。你会被推向极限,如果不够专注就会犯下危险的错误。在享受极限运动时学会如此专注将帮助你在工作中保持专注,使你更高效,最终更成功。

transcript.en: It's great to stay fit and healthy, but standard exercise routines and sports only work the same muscles repeatedly. With extreme sports, you'll be working entirely different muscles, and that means you get an all-over workout. Extreme sports also burn a lot more calories than other sports. Skateboarding, for example, can burn as many as 500 calories per hour. Basketball burns around 300 in the same time.
transcript.zh: 保持健康很重要,但标准的锻炼程序和运动只会反复锻炼相同的肌肉。通过极限运动,你会锻炼到完全不同的肌肉,这意味着你能得到全身锻炼。极限运动消耗的卡路里也比其他运动多得多。例如,滑板每小时可以消耗多达500卡路里,而篮球在同样时间内消耗约300卡路里。

transcript.en: When you find that you can overcome the physical or mental challenges involved in extreme sports, you'll feel superhuman and your self-confidence will be at an all-time high.
transcript.zh: 当你发现自己能够克服极限运动中的身体或心理挑战时,你会感觉自己无所不能,自信心将达到前所未有的高度。

transcript.en: Most of us have been in teams or organizations where we've had conflict with the people that we're working with around the ideas or decisions that we're discussing. Conflict is natural. We all bring different life and work experiences to the table. We all have different personality preferences and tendencies. We're not all going to have the same ideas on how to approach policies, programs or problems.
transcript.zh: 我们大多数人都曾身处这样的团队或组织：在讨论想法或决策时，与合作者产生冲突。冲突是自然的。我们每个人都带来不同的生活和工作经验。我们都有不同的性格偏好和倾向。我们不可能在如何处理政策、项目或问题上都有相同的想法。

transcript.en: But too often we get caught in this place where conflict is perceived to be negative—something we want to avoid so that we can maintain the harmony of our workplace. This could be because some people want to avoid conflict at all costs, after all they still have to work together. But this kind of artificial harmony isn't the answer.
transcript.zh: 但我们经常陷入这样一种境地：冲突被视为负面的——我们想要避免的东西，以便维持工作场所的和谐。这可能是因为有些人想不惜一切代价避免冲突,毕竟他们还要继续共事。但这种人为的和谐并不是答案。

transcript.en: Productive conflict is a vital part of teams and organizations that want to push forward and do more. Without conflict, we're often stuck in this artificial harmony where people don't express potentially innovative ideas for fear that they may start conflict with others.
transcript.zh: 建设性冲突是想要向前推进并做得更多的团队和组织的重要组成部分。没有冲突,我们往往会陷入这种人为的和谐,人们不敢表达可能具有创新性的想法,因为担心可能会与他人产生冲突。

transcript.en: But if you're in a place where you have a basis of trust, conflict can be extremely productive. It can lead to increased innovation and greater trust on teams. It may be an uncomfortable process, but good leaders and healthy teams recognize that productive and healthy conflict is an important part of how they function.
transcript.zh: 但如果你所在的地方有信任的基础,冲突可以极具建设性。它可以带来更多创新和团队间更大的信任。这可能是一个令人不适的过程,但优秀的领导者和健康的团队认识到,建设性和健康的冲突是他们运作方式的重要组成部分。

matching.title: No escape as 'snow day' becomes 'e-learning day'

paragraphs.t: Certain institutions, such as schools, are likely to close when bad weather, such as snow, flooding or extreme heat or cold, causes travel difficulties, power outages( 断供), or otherwise endangers public safety. When snowy weather arrives in the US, it means the chance of school children benefiting from the long-standing tradition of the "snow day", when schools are forced to close and students get an unexpected day off.

The criterion for a snow day is primarily the inability of school buses to operate safely on their routes and danger to children who walk to school. Often, the school remains officially open even though buses do not run and classes are canceled. Severe weather that causes cancellation or delay is more likely in regions that are less able to handle the situation. Snow days are less common in more northern areas of the United States that are used to heavy winter snowfall, because municipalities are well equipped to clear roads and remove snow. In areas less accustomed to snow even small snowfalls of an inch or two may render roads unsafe.

Snow days are a familiar theme in American film and TV shows, with children getting the good news and then running outside for some seasonal snowman-building and snowball throwing, against a background of joyful pop music. But the tradition is now over for pupils in several US states such as South Carolina, Nevada, Georgia and Indiana. This academic year, many school boards have introduced policies which require students to work from home if the school is shut by snow or extreme weather. They are known as "e- learning days", which certainly sounds less fun than a snow day.

Teachers are also losing their snow days and instead will be expected to be on hand to take a virtual register and answer students' questions online. A pilot programme in a school district in Anderson County, South Carolina, has supplied students with electronic tablets loaded with assignments to complete in the event of a school closure. If it is successful, it could be rolled out across the state.

But some parents object to the new policy if the vigorous debate on the Facebook page of Anderson County school district is anything to go by. "When it snows, let the kids enjoy it," said one commenter. Another said the decision would "ruin school even more", and someone else called snow days "a fun part of childhood". But supporters of the policy say it means children will miss fewer days of school. It will also bring to an end a less popular US high school tradition: the "make-up day", which requires students in many states to make up the time lost due to weather by working during school holidays.

Students in North Carolina already have several make-up days scheduled because of school closures during Hurricane Florence, which struck in September. Tom Wilson, the superintendent(主管) of Anderson County school district, said the change away from snow days makes practical and financial sense. He said technology has changed every profession, so it makes sense to use it to "eliminate" make-up days. Adam Baker of the Department of Education in Indiana said e-learning days were proving a "great success". He said most Indiana schools already use digital devices during lessons, so it was an "easy decision" to extend this to days when schools are closed. He denies the decision is depriving children of the chance to enjoy the snow. "Students are still able to enjoy snow days and outside time," he said. "Many have PE and science assignments that have them out enjoying the weather." But local school superintendents in Ohio are resisting proposals to adopt e-learning days. They fear that students without internet access at home will be disadvantaged by the policy, and superintendent Tom Roth is concerned that e-learning days will offer a lower quality of education.

There are also so-called "blizzard bags", with assignments that children take home ahead of an expected snow closure. But Mr Roth says it is not sufficient as a replacement. "I think we still need the class time to give our kids the education that they deserve," he said. "You can't get that with a blizzard bag or doing the work from home like that. It's not going to be as effective."

There is a long-running debate on whether missing days of school affects attainment. In England, there has been a focus on tackling absenteeism(旷课) from school. The Department for Education (DFE) published research in 2016 arguing that missing any days at school could have a negative impact on results. Even a few days lost in a year could be enough to miss out on getting a good exam grade, the DFE's research concluded. This differed from the findings of a study from Harvard University in the US, which concluded that missing a few occasional days because of the weather did not damage learning.

The Harvard study examined seven years of school results data and could not find any impact from snow closures. What caused more disruption was when schools tried to stay open in bad weather, even though many staff and pupils were absent. But weather can make a difference to school results, according to another piece of Harvard research published last summer. It's hot weather that has the negative impact. The results of 10 million school students were examined over 13 years and researchers found a "significant" link between years with extremely hot weather and lower results.

It's obvious that students should go to school every day to get the most out of education. In cases of extreme weather students don't always have that option. However, research shows that authorised absences from school such as during extreme weather are less problematic for students than absences that are not authorised. This is because unauthorised absences tend to reflect patterns and behaviours of student disengagement, or the possible negative attitudes of parents towards education that students adopt and carry with them through schooling. The level of impact on students' educational performance is all to do with the length of time that a student is absent from school and how regularly this occurs.

careful.passage: It may sound surprising, but you don't have to be interested in fashion, or even in history, to enjoy Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History. I happen to be interested in both, and ended up enjoying the book for completely different reasons. Richard Thompson Ford is a law professor, and you probably won't forget that for even one page. His carefully reasoned arguments, packed with examples, sound almost like reading a court opinion, only maybe wordier. You will probably never think of fashion as a trifle again. Ford's thesis is that the best way to understand what particular fashions meant in any given era is to look at the restrictions placed on them. Through this lens, he shows us that the first laws passed in the 1200s to ensure that only the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments reflected the rise of the middle class, who were now able to imitate some of these fashions. The status of the upper classes was threatened; fashion was a tool to preserve it. Ford takes the reader through the evolution of fashion while examining the underlying motivations of status, sex, power, and personality, which, he assumes, influenced all innovations in fashion in the past and which continue to influence us today. His writing is more than a little dense—dense with research, clauses, and precise adjectives and nouns. But there's also humor and enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing. No one is spared his sharp analysis: not the easy targets of 19th century women's crippling(伤害身体的) fashions nor the modern uniforms of Silicon Valley T-shirts But the greatest strength of this book (on fashion!) is its intellectual profoundness. Ford asks us to question unconscious beliefs, to realize that we almost never do so, to understand that the simplest choices are charged with meaning, and yet that meaning can and does change all the time. Consider the fact that a 1918 catalog insisted that boys and girls be dressed in the appropriate color. We believe our thinking today is evolved; Ford shows us it's not.

careful.passage: The art of persuasion means convincing others to agree with your point of view or to follow your course of action. For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes naturally. For the rest of us, persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time. Employers place a great value on employees with persuasion skills because they can impact several aspects of job performance. Besides, teamwork and leadership rely heavily on the power of persuasion to get things done. Without persuasion skills, employees may not be as committed to or convinced of the importance of an organization's vision and long-term mission. Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your ideas, it'll also help you motivate them to achieve a common goal. In order to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace, you need to understand how to handle conflicts and reach agreements. Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just as important. Before you can get somebody on-board with your goal, you should help them understand why they should pursue it. Using visual aids to back up your ideas can help communicate your ideas better and make compelling arguments so your listeners will come to a logical choice and become fully committed to your ideas and plans. Successful persuasion skills are based on your ability to have positive interactions and maintain meaningful relationships with people. In order to sustain those relationships, you must be able to work in their best interests as well. Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you. The more they achieve and the greater progress they make, the more they trust your judgement and strength. We persuade and get persuaded every day—we're either convincing or being convinced. A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational structures; no one likes to be told what to do or to be pushed around. Therefore, organizations and leaders should adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes.

translation.source: 汉语中的 "福"字 (the character fu)表示幸福和好运,是中国传统文化中最常用的吉祥(auspicious) 符号之 一。人们通常将一个大大的福字写在红纸上, 寓意期盼家庭幸福、社会安定、国家昌盛。春节贴福字是民间由 来已久的习俗。为了欢庆春节, 家家户户都会将福字贴在门上或墙上, 表达对幸福生活的向往、对美好未来的 期待。人们有时还将福字倒过来贴，表示幸福已到、好运已到。
translation.reference: The Chinese character "Fu" means happiness and good fortune, and is one of the most commonly used auspicious symbols in traditional Chinese culture. People usually write a large character "Fu" on red paper, expressing their wish for family happiness, social stability and national prosperity. Pasting the character "Fu" during the Spring Festival is a long-standing folk custom. To celebrate the Spring Festival, every household pastes the character "Fu" on doors or walls, expressing their longing for a happy life and their expectation for a better future. Sometimes people also paste the character "Fu" upside down to indicate that happiness and good fortune have arrived.
